sections.html:
There isn't one. Act 645 of 2003 repealed the state estate tax, and no Arkansas estate tax return is required for anyone who died after December 31, 2004.

For an heir holding a house, that settles the first worry. The state doesn't take a share of the estate based on its size, and there is no Arkansas estate tax return to file. The Department of Finance and Administration publishes a one-page repeal notice, and it is worth printing for the probate file if a title company or lender asks.

That notice covers the estate tax only. An heir with a large inheritance can ask a probate attorney to confirm the details before distribution.

The federal tax reaches only very large estates. A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, is above the filing threshold for the year of death. That threshold is $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026.

Most relatively simple estates never need to file. When one does, the gross estate is valued at fair market value on the date of death, and deductions can include mortgages and other debts, estate administration expenses, property passing to a surviving spouse and qualified charities. A surviving spouse may also elect to carry over the decedent's unused exemption, known as portability, on a timely filed return.

sections.h2: Income tax when an heir sells
sections.html:
Often very little, since the heir's basis usually starts at the home's value when the owner died. Publication 551 treats fair market value on the date of death as the basis of inherited property, or the value on the alternate valuation date if the personal representative elects it. Heirs who receive a Schedule A (Form 8971) generally use the estate tax value reported there.

Gain runs from that starting figure up to the sale price. A house that sells for about its date-of-death value tends to produce a small gain. One that rises in value while the heir waits produces a gain equal to the increase. Arkansas then taxes only half of a net long-term gain.

Income the estate itself earns, such as rent collected before the sale, is a separate matter. The Department of Finance and Administration keeps a page of fiduciary and estate income tax forms for personal representatives.

sections.h2: Skipping formal probate with a small estate
sections.html:
When the estate is small, a distributee can collect and distribute assets without a personal representative. Ark. Code 28-41-101 sets the limit at $100,000 of property owned at death, less encumbrances. The decedent's homestead and any statutory allowances for a surviving spouse or minor children don't count toward that figure.

That carve-out helps with houses. A family home that was the decedent's homestead doesn't use up the $100,000, though it still appears in the affidavit.

  • At least 45 days must pass after the death.
  • No petition for appointment of a personal representative can be pending or granted.
  • One or more distributees file an affidavit with the probate clerk of the circuit court in the proper county.
  • The affidavit states that there are no unpaid claims, and that the Department of Human Services either furnished no benefits or has been reimbursed.
  • It lists personal property with values, and real property by legal description with value, including the homestead.
  • The clerk charges $25 to file and $5 per certified copy, with no extra fee if a will is attached.

sections.h2: Extra steps when real property is involved
sections.html:
Within 30 days after filing, the distributee must publish a notice of the death and the affidavit. Creditors then have three months from the first publication to present verified claims, and late claims are barred.

Plan a sale around that three-month window. A buyer or title company may want proof that the affidavit was filed, the notice ran and the claims period ended before a deed is signed. The distributee may also open a bank account in the estate's name without a petition or court order, which helps for holding sale proceeds and paying final bills.

Estates above the limit, or with a dispute among heirs, go through regular administration in the circuit court's probate division. That route has its own filings, and a probate attorney can explain which one fits.

sections.h2: Costs of transferring or selling the house
sections.html:
The main closing cost the state adds is the real property transfer tax: $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on a deed or instrument conveying realty, on transactions over $100. Ark. Code 26-60-105 splits it into $1.10 per $1,000 and an added $2.20 per $1,000 paid by the purchaser.

Property tax follows the house too. Under Ark. Code 26-36-201, real property tax is payable to the county collector from the first business day of March through October 15. Anything unpaid after October 15 is delinquent and carries a 10% penalty. An estate still settling in the fall should check that the current bill hasn't slipped.

Utilities, insurance and upkeep continue until the deed is recorded, so a vacant inherited house can run up costs even when the estate owes no tax.

Begin by confirming who legally owns the house and what has to be filed, then decide whether to keep, rent or sell.

  • Locate the will, the deed and the latest property tax statement.
  • Ask the county assessor or collector for the parcel's tax status.
  • Check whether the estate qualifies for the small estate affidavit or needs a personal representative.
  • Get a date-of-death value in writing, since it sets the basis for any later sale.
  • Secure the house and keep insurance active.
  • Speak with a probate attorney and a tax professional before signing a sale contract.

Heirs who live out of state, or who inherited a house needing repairs, sometimes choose a cash sale to avoid carrying costs and repair projects. The right choice depends on the estate's papers and the family's timeline.

faqs.q: Is there an Arkansas estate tax?
faqs.a: No. Act 645 of 2003 repealed it, and no estate tax return is required for decedents who died after December 31, 2004.

faqs.q: Do heirs owe tax on income the estate earns before the house sells?
faqs.a: That is a separate matter from the estate tax. The Department of Finance and Administration keeps a page of fiduciary and estate income tax forms for personal representatives.

faqs.q: At what size does the federal estate tax apply?
faqs.a: A federal return is required when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death. That threshold is $15,000,000 for 2026.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas small estate limit?
faqs.a: Property owned at death, less encumbrances, can be up to $100,000, not counting the homestead and statutory allowances for a surviving spouse or minor children. At least 45 days must pass after death. Creditors then have three months from first publication of the notice, which must run within 30 days after the affidavit is filed.

faqs.q: Will I owe tax if I sell an inherited house right away?
faqs.a: Usually little, since the basis is the fair market value at the date of death. The gain is the sale price minus that figure, and Arkansas taxes half of a net long-term gain.
